concepts.name: Outrigger
concepts.prompt:
Create one landscape concept illustration of an original SMALL starter utility cargo spaceship for a cozy space trucking game, roughly 12–15 metres long with a single walkable deck, tiny living quarters, cockpit, bathroom and modest enclosed cargo hold. This is one of five NEW designs after earlier rounded camper-like ships were rejected. User preferred asymmetry and closely joined twin hulls. Push intentional industrial design and striking silhouette: contrasting beveled angular pressure shells and selected curved corners, stepped volumes, recessed mechanical junctions, strong purposeful shapes, negative space. NOT an RV, bus, rounded loaf, airplane, fighter, warship or huge freighter.
Art: Moebius-inspired fine ink and painted European science fiction comic illustration. Broad clear matte color planes, restrained hand painted variation, fine selective navy contours, warm cream sunlight with crisp cool blue shadows. Cassette futurism, inset CRT cockpit hardware, tactile mechanisms, few meaningful details, minimal weathering. NOT photoreal, no gritty realism, no dense random greebles, no thick black cartoon outlines. No text, titles, logos or annotations.
Show whole ship in a compelling elevated three-quarter view with all landing feet visible, generous margins, on a very simple pale orbital hangar floor with a dark blue space opening far behind. Ship dominant, background quiet. Include one adult worker and two hand-carried crates for scale. Small loading ramp and plausible cabin windows communicate usable space. Keep human-scale door approximately 2m high. No weapons, no long wings, no giant windows, no sprawling shipping containers. Main engines exhaust aft, maneuvering thrusters small and physically meaningful. Warm inhabited window, restrained work lamps. This is fresh concept art, not a game screenshot.

Specific design:
A beautifully asymmetric narrow wedge cockpit/hab keel on the left and a shorter chunky rectangular cargo capsule tucked to its right, connected by a substantial enclosed transverse passage and rear machinery block. The cabin nose is faceted and overhangs a recessed chin like a compact deep-sea research vessel; cargo front sits 3m farther back with a small forward ramp. A visible narrow slot of shadow separates the forward hull volumes. Low lengthwise stance, tapered aft drive housings, inset side radiator. Deep petrol blue main cabin, chalk ivory cargo pod, small vermilion hatch accent. Front left view. Deliberate elegant asymmetry, slim profile but walkable headroom.

Cockpit is inset at front of LEFT pod, not a bubble stuck between pods. A tightly integrated L-shaped asymmetric space hauler. Short broad faceted cargo body forms the rear crossbar, narrow forward cockpit and living cabin extends out from the left side, right front is recessed into a sheltered loading alcove. A low fold-down ramp leads from that alcove into the rear hold, naturally protected by the projecting hab beside it. No exposed deck or open cargo, all living and cargo volumes enclosed and walkable. Sidewall panel planes lean slightly inward; chunky chamfered corners, a single slim oval hab porthole, rear engine block low and broad. Pale warm grey with muted wine-red cabin roof and charcoal recesses, tiny faded teal service panel. Front-right view emphasizes the offset front and sheltered cargo entry. Compact, confident and appealing, not boxy bus.

Specific design:
A compact distinctive twin-boom utility spaceship with an enclosed central living/cargo pressure cabin nestled between two shorter slim ENGINE outriggers. The central hull is a tallish flattened hexagonal wedge, with an inset forward cockpit and a continuous hab behind, offset side ramp aft. Twin engine outriggers hug its sides only along rear half, form open slots around the central spine, held by robust short brackets rather than wings. Two cylindrical aft-facing thruster nozzles inside squared protective jackets. Cockpit forward glass is narrow three-piece angular inset, one modest living porthole; walkable central hull tall enough and no excessive volume. Four stubby landing legs. Dusty sage and warm ivory central shell, dark indigo engine casings, restrained golden yellow trim. Front-left high three-quarter view. Sophisticated industrial compactness, interesting exposed structural joins, graceful balanced proportions.

A remarkably compact asymmetric manta-like freighter with a broad diamond-shaped chamfered pressure shell, no wings, no pointed nose. One narrow projecting rectangular cockpit prow on front left, opposite it a deeply inset front-right freight hatch/ramp; pressure hull bridges them behind to make an almost horseshoe footprint. Cabin roof has a stepped off-center dorsal machinery ridge, cockpit and living window on left; small hold on right. Back edge is squared off with two recessed rectangular aft engines, a slim radiator panel flush in roof. Landing legs tuck into four corners, low and sturdy. Warm ivory with muted ochre main roof plane and dark slate-blue forward cockpit, minimal red hatch edge. Front three-quarter showing its unusual divided nose and continuous rear body. Graphic silhouette, purposeful negative space, not a saucer, not a military fighter.
